places.now: the Thames, tidal through central London; this point is the Pool of London reach by London Bridge
places.reason: The river is a line, not a point; the point is a representative one for the reach that most of Dickens's London scenes use, and it is not tied to any particular passage.

places.now: Brighton, part of the city of Brighton and Hove, East Sussex
places.reason: A well-known seaside town; the hospital match is a spurious place-level result.

places.now: demolished 1902; the Central Criminal Court (Old Bailey) stands on the site at Newgate Street and Old Bailey
places.reason: Newgate stood at the corner of Newgate Street and Old Bailey, and the Old Bailey was built on its site.

places.now: no known real street; fictional
places.reason: Brig Place is Dickens's invention for Captain Cuttle's lodgings near the docks and Wooden Midshipman, and no real street is clearly identified.

places.now: vanished court; the site is around Cursitor Street off Chancery Lane (Holborn)
places.reason: Cook's Court was a real small court off Cursitor Street, Chancery Lane (Snagsby's law-stationer's shop), though the exact spot is approximate.

places.now: the Caribbean islands (Jamaica, Barbados, Antigua and others)
places.reason: A region, not a point; the coordinates are an approximate centre of the Caribbean island arc.

places.now: Barnard's Inn Hall, Holborn, owned by Gresham College
places.reason: A well-documented former Inn of Chancery on the south side of Holborn near Fetter Lane, and the hall survives.

places.now: Royal Victoria and Bull Hotel, High Street, Rochester (the Bull Inn, which probably inspired the Blue Boar)
places.reason: The Blue Boar is a fictionalised Rochester inn modelled on the Bull Inn on Rochester High Street, so the spot is approximate.

places.now: Buckingham Street, WC2, running from the Strand down to Victoria Embankment Gardens
places.reason: A real street in the Adelphi district; Dickens himself lodged at no. 15 in the 1830s and the street still exists.

places.now: High Street, Rochester, Kent
places.reason: Pumblechook's premises are in the High Street of Dickens's Rochester-based market town, but the exact building is not identifiable; the gazetteer's ME2 postcode suggests it matched Strood instead.

places.now: no known real place; fictional
places.reason: Princess's Place (Miss Tox's retreat) is Dickens's invention, with no secure real location, and the Marylebone match is only a name resemblance.

places.now: probably the Grapes pub, Narrow Street, Limehouse (the usual identification)
places.reason: The pub is fictional but commonly identified with the Grapes at 76 Narrow Street, Limehouse.

places.now: now part of Holborn Viaduct, running between Holborn Circus and Farringdon Street
places.reason: Holborn Hill was the steep descent to the Fleet valley, largely superseded by the Holborn Viaduct (1869).

places.now: fictional; no real building, so the point is only the Brighton seafront
places.reason: Dr Blimber's is a fictional school in Brighton, located only loosely on the seafront.

places.now: fictional; no real equivalent
places.reason: Boffin's Bower is a fictional house set among the dust-heaps on the Harmon estate, with no securely identified location.

places.now: demolished 1880; the site lies between Borough Road and Newington Causeway (Southwark), near Harper Road
places.reason: The King's Bench Prison stood in Southwark's St George's Fields, and its site is well documented.

places.now: fictional; the point is only central Brighton seafront
places.reason: Mrs Pipchin's 'Castle' is a fictional Brighton boarding house, located only loosely on the seafront.

places.now: demolished (c. 1870s); site is on Chancery Lane near Cursitor Street, now offices
places.reason: Symond's Inn was a real Inn of Chancery on Chancery Lane, and the exact position is approximate.

places.now: Thavies Inn, a small street off Holborn Circus, with modern buildings
places.reason: Thavies Inn was a real Inn of Chancery near Holborn Circus, and the name survives on the street.

places.now: Twickenham, in the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames
places.reason: A well-known town on the Thames in Middlesex; the hospital match is just a place-level mismatch.

places.now: Albany, a residential set of chambers off Piccadilly
places.reason: A well-documented building complex on the north side of Piccadilly, which survives.

places.now: fictional pub; the point is only the Hoo/Cooling marsh area of Kent
places.reason: The Jolly Bargemen is a fictional pub in the village of Pip's Kent marsh country, which Dickens based on the Cooling and Hoo area.

places.now: fictional; no real shop is identified
places.reason: The Wooden Midshipman is a fictional instrument shop in the City near the docks, and the exact location is not given.

places.now: around Mill Pond, near Bermondsey Wall and Rotherhithe; much redeveloped
places.reason: Mill Pond Bank and Chinks's Basin are fictionalised, perhaps based on the Mill Pond area at Bermondsey/Rotherhithe.

places.now: site of the Marshalsea Prison, off Borough High Street (Southwark); only a wall and a small park remain
places.reason: The Snuggery was a tap-room inside the real Marshalsea, so the spot is approximate for the prison site.
